provenance.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE finished landscape 4:3 bird portrait for the Birdsong-to-Art collection, filling the image as beautifully as these approved references. Never a grid, contact sheet or storyboard.
REFERENCE ROLES: image 1 is the primary original family style; image 2 supplies expressive contours and printed colour; image 3 supplies sophisticated close-up feather detail; image 4 calibrates clearer graphic feather groups and selective edge contrast. Use these for ARTISTIC LANGUAGE ONLY. Draw the new species' own anatomy and identifying marks.
MEDIUM AND FINISH: warm ivory cold-pressed paper, translucent watercolour underpainting, rich print/gouache-like pigment, broken dry-print grain, economical expressive ink contours, sharp directional coloured-pencil drawing. The bird must read as designed shapes as well as fine texture: clear pigment masses, rhythmic overlapping feather groups, selective dark separations and pale feather edges. Precise detailing lives within larger readable shapes; quiet body passages contrast with intricate focal work. Keep the finish rich and detailed like the originals. No uniform microtexture, photographic airbrushed shading, blanket heavy outline, flat vector simplification or glossy mascot eyes.
CHARACTER: modest expressive stylisation through posture, contour, balance and drawing rhythm while preserving species anatomy. A little surprise in the authored drawing is welcome. No human eyebrows, grin, props, costume, joke, fact caption or repeated literal leaf badge. Do not copy the reference birds' body proportions, yellow beaks, pink legs or eye colours.
COMPOSITION: single dominant whole bird, comfortably inside the landscape frame including full bill, toes and tail. Species-led plumage colours, exposed paper, spare ink support. Simple abstract background shapes only; their precise outline, crop and placement can be invented within the direction below. Material texture compatible with the bird, subordinate to it; no detailed habitat, foliage, building, scenic landscape or ornate frame.
LETTERING: only the exact name supplied below, understated legible dark handwritten lettering beneath the bird. Lower-right corner empty: no sensor state, icon, number or invented encounter data. No signature/watermark or extra text.
SUBJECT: Redwing (Turdus iliacus), Adult Redwing, sex unspecified, typical winter visitor.
VERIFIED IDENTIFIERS TO PRESERVE:
- Small thrush with warm/dark brown upperparts and a conspicuous creamy-white eyebrow extending behind the dark eye.
- Cream underside with dark brown streaking; orange-rust flank patch below the folded wing, and matching rusty underwing if exposed.
- Slender pointed bill with yellowish base and dark distal portion; dark eyes, muted fleshy-brown legs; brown tail.
Avoid identity confusion: Red wing-coverts or fully red upperwing: the namesake red is mainly flank/underwing; A plain Song Thrush face without bold eyebrow; Blue-grey head and rump of Fieldfare; Round decorative polka dots replacing directional breast streaking
ARTISTIC POSE: A compact thrush facing right in a light forward ground step, head inclined slightly as if attending to something nearby. Show one full flank and wing; keep the tail modest and lowered.
SPECIFIC DRAWING EMPHASIS: Bold pale eyebrow and malar stripe, brown upperparts, streaked pale breast and true rusty-red flank patch. Let fine warm brown feather drawing and the red flank carry the colour; no all-red breast or blue-grey head.
BACKGROUND DIRECTION: Two broad unequal pale olive pigment planes with a diagonal white gap, quiet and spacious behind the warm flank.
PLUMAGE PALETTE: brown, cream, rusty red flank, dark brown streaks. Keep the biology legible; colour accents are in mark-making, not replacements for identifying markings.
TEXT VERBATIM: "Redwing".
